subsystems.name: Neural signal acquisition
subsystems.role: captures the electrical activity that the key would be derived from.
parts: EEG electrodes (wet, dry or implanted arrays)
shielding against mains and muscle artefact

subsystems.name: Feature extraction
subsystems.role: turns raw microvolt-scale waveforms into stable numbers that differ between people.

subsystems.name: Entropy and stability analysis
subsystems.role: asks the decisive question — how many unpredictable bits does a recording actually contain, and can they be reproduced?
parts: within-person repeatability testing across days and sessions

subsystems.name: Key derivation
subsystems.role: converts noisy, non-identical measurements into an exactly reproducible key.
parts: cryptographic hash to a fixed-length key

subsystems.name: Authentication protocol
subsystems.role: uses the derived key for a real security purpose.
parts: challenge task presented to the user
integration with standard ciphers such as AES

subsystems.name: Spoofing defence
subsystems.role: stops an attacker recording or synthesising the signal.

buildSteps.title: Pick the signal and the task
buildSteps.detail: Choose between scalp EEG, which is non-invasive but coarse, and implanted electrodes, which are sharp but surgical. Then choose a repeatable mental task — imagined movement, a mental arithmetic challenge, or a visual stimulus — so the response is comparable between sessions.

buildSteps.title: Collect longitudinal data
buildSteps.detail: Record the same person many times over weeks, in different moods and states, and record many other people. Single-session results are meaningless here; the whole problem is reproducibility.

buildSteps.title: Extract candidate features
buildSteps.detail: Filter the signal, remove eye-blink and muscle artefact, and compute features such as band power or evoked-response shape at specific electrodes and time windows.

buildSteps.title: Select features that are personal and stable
buildSteps.detail: Keep only features that stay close to the same value for one person over time yet differ clearly between people. In practice the candidate pool shrinks a lot at this step.

buildSteps.title: Measure real entropy
buildSteps.detail: Estimate how many genuinely unpredictable bits a recording provides. This is the step that decides whether the idea can work at all, and results so far are modest compared with the length of the recording.

buildSteps.title: Build the error-correcting layer
buildSteps.detail: Because two recordings are never bit-identical, wrap the features in a fuzzy extractor or secure sketch: enrolment produces helper data, and each later reading is corrected back to the same value.

buildSteps.title: Derive a key with a standard cipher
buildSteps.detail: Hash the corrected value into an AES key or similar, and use it inside an ordinary authentication protocol rather than inventing a new cipher.

buildSteps.title: Attack your own system
buildSteps.detail: Attempt replay from a prior recording, synthetic signal generation, coercion of the user, and cross-session drift. Any of these breaks the scheme in real use.

buildSteps.title: Decide what it is actually for
buildSteps.detail: Realistically the outcome is a second or third authentication factor for a narrow setting, not a replacement for public-key cryptography.

prerequisites.why: research-grade EEG exists; consumer headsets are noisy, and implanted arrays need surgery and degrade over time.

prerequisites.tech: Biometric key derivation (fuzzy extractors, secure sketches)
prerequisites.why: the mathematics for turning noisy biometric readings into reproducible keys is already established, and would be reused here.
keys require bit-exact reproduction, but neural activity varies with attention, fatigue, caffeine and time of day — the central unsolved problem.
a key is only as strong as its unpredictable content, and most of an EEG trace is either predictable or shared across people.
recordings can be captured and replayed, so liveness tests are essential for any security claim.

pathway.milestone: research on EEG-based person identification and, separately, on neural-information security
pathway.unlocks: evidence about how distinguishable and how stable individual brain signals are.

pathway.milestone: lab prototype that derives a reproducible key with published entropy estimates and a defined threat model
pathway.unlocks: an honest answer to whether the entropy is enough to be worth using.

pathway.milestone: challenge–response authentication demonstrated against replay and synthesis attacks
pathway.unlocks: possible use as a supplementary factor in high-assurance settings, alongside a password or hardware token.

pathway.milestone: if stable, high-capacity neural interfaces become routine, key material drawn from brain activity could become a niche factor
pathway.unlocks: a convenience layer for implanted-device users — but ordinary cryptographic keys do the real work, and are far cheaper and faster.
